before:
Tidal Slipway — Allocation of Winter Hauling Slots

The harbour committee reminds members that the slipway cradle takes one vessel at a time between November and February. Where more than one request is received for the same tide, the yard foreman works down the standing order of claim: working fishing craft are hauled before club training gigs, and club training gigs before privately owned pleasure boats. Every craft on the register remains entitled to a haul during the season, and no request is refused on grounds of category. Members should submit the pink docket to the harbour office at least nine days before the tide they want. Late dockets are held over to the following spring tide and dealt with in the same way.

before:
Bothy Wardens' Handbook — Section 7, The Lower Room Stove

Section 7 covers the cast-iron stove in the lower room of the bothy. Wardens are permitted to light the stove at any hour during the winter months, provided the flue damper is opened fully and the ash pan is emptied before the fire is laid. Coal is not carried in; visitors bring their own fuel or use the driftwood stack under the porch. The warden on duty checks the chimney sweep card in the tin box by the door and enters the date of the last sweep in the visitors' book. If the card is missing, the warden telephones the association secretary from the call box at the road end before any fire is lit.
after:
Bothy Wardens' Handbook — Section 7, The Lower Room Stove

Section 7 covers the cast-iron stove in the lower room of the bothy. Wardens must not light the stove between midnight and six in the morning during the winter months, provided the flue damper is opened fully and the ash pan is emptied before the fire is laid. Coal is not carried in; visitors bring their own fuel or use the driftwood stack under the porch. The warden on duty checks the chimney sweep card in the tin box by the door and enters the date of the last sweep in the visitors' book. If the card is missing, the warden telephones the association secretary from the call box at the road end before any fire is lit.
variation_site: The alteration falls in the sentence about lighting the stove in winter.
author_note: A permission is converted into a prohibition over part of the day.

before:
Lock-Keeper's Day Log — Entry for 14 March

Wind north-east, moderate; four ascents and three descents worked between first light and dusk. Two narrowboats waited above the top gate for the water to come round from the feeder. The standing note pinned inside the lid of this log was copied out again this morning after the old card went soft with damp, and now reads: would crews please refrain from running engines while the chamber is filling. The offside gate paddle remains stiff and was greased at noon. The gauge board was wiped and read at eight and again at four, and both figures were entered on the weekly return sent to the navigation office.

before:
County Herbarium — Collections Policy, Section 4

Section 4 sets out how the herbarium's older accessions are held. The Marsh Lane holdings, some six hundred sheets gathered between the wars, are designated a teaching collection, and that designation governs which store they occupy and which loan form applies. Sheets in the west range are kept at twelve degrees with the blinds drawn from April to September. Requests from outside the county are answered within twenty working days, and a sheet leaves the building only in the flat box with the tape seal. Curatorial staff review each designation once every five years and report the outcome to the trustees at the autumn meeting.

before:
Reservoir Draw-Down — Interim Silt Note

This interim note accompanies the draw-down carried out over the last fortnight. Probing was done from the punt on a ten-metre grid, with a graduated pole and a plate foot. Silt depth at the northern inlet is 1.4 metres, falling to under half a metre off the valve tower. The eastern shallows could not be reached because of standing reed. Water clarity was poor throughout and the plate was more often felt than seen. A fuller survey with the echo sounder is proposed for the dry spell in late summer, and the committee is asked to note the figures below before deciding on dredging in the winter.

before:
Weather Station Alpha — Site Configuration Sheet

This sheet holds the fixed entries typed into the logger at the field station above the quarry. Station elevation is entered as thirty-four metres above ordnance datum, taken from the surveyor's mark on the gatepost. Anemometer height is three metres on the mast, and the rain gauge rim sits half a metre above the turf. The logger writes a line every ten minutes to the card and clears the buffer at midnight. Battery voltage is written alongside each line so that flat cells can be spotted from the office. Whoever swaps the card initials this sheet in the margin and posts the old card to the county office in the padded envelope.

before:
Brass Band — Sectional Rehearsal Arrangements

Sectionals run on the Tuesday before each contest and are taken by the section leaders rather than the conductor. Players arrive for seven, tune to the bandroom piano, and work through the marked passages in the parts already handed out. The cornets and flugel use the committee room at the back of the institute, and the low brass stay in the bandroom itself. Percussion work with whichever section needs them and are excused when nobody does. Stands and lamps are put back on the rack at the end, and the caretaker locks up at half past nine. Anyone unable to attend tells their own section leader and not the secretary.

before:
Burial Ground Registry — Entering a New Interment

The clerk enters each interment in the bound register in the following working sequence. The grave number is copied from the sexton's chit, then the name and dates are written in ink from the certificate, then the plan sheet in the drawer is shaded and initialled, and last the index card is typed and filed. Nothing in the bound register is erased; an error is ruled through once and initialled in the margin. The register stays in the safe overnight and is produced for the parish clerk at the quarterly meeting. Families asking for a copy of an entry are given the printed extract form, which the clerk completes from the register and never from the index card.

before:
Tide Gauge Manual — Format of the Daily Return

Returns are sent nightly as a plain text file to the district office. Each line carries the station code, the reading time, the height in metres and the quality mark, separated by commas, with no header line and no trailing comma. Times are given on the twenty-four hour clock and heights to two decimal places. A missing reading is sent as an empty field rather than a zero, so that the office can tell a gap from a low water. Files are named for the station and the date. If the line to the office is down, the operator keeps the file on the machine and sends the backlog when the link returns; nothing is retyped by hand.
after:
Tide Gauge Manual — Format of the Daily Return

Each line carries the station code, the reading time, the height in metres and the quality mark, separated by tab characters, with a single heading line and no trailing tab. Times are given on the twenty-four hour clock and heights to two decimal places. A missing reading is sent as an empty field rather than a zero, so that the office can tell a gap from a low water. Files are named for the station and the date. If the line to the office is down, the operator keeps the file on the machine and sends the backlog when the link returns; nothing is retyped by hand.
variation_site: The alteration falls in the sentence describing how the fields on each line are laid out.
author_note: The encoding of the return changes while the content a reader takes from it is the same.

before:
Seed Bank Bulletin — The Accession Year

Growers are reminded that the accession year begins on 1 October and runs to 30 September. Every count in this bulletin follows that boundary: the germination tables, the store audit, the lending totals and the ten-year trend chart are all cut at the same date, and a sample lifted in late September belongs to the year then closing. Growers sending in material near the boundary should write the collection date on the packet so that the store clerk can place it correctly. The back pages carry last year's figures alongside for comparison, and any restatement will be shown in italics with a note beneath the table.
